title: The Free WiFi Trap
topicTitle: Public WiFi is not automatically private
topicBrief: On an untrusted network, an attacker may sit between your device and a website. A Man-in-the-Middle attack can alter pages, downgrade a secure connection, or steal credentials. Check the address and certificate before signing in. This is a fictional, offline simulation.
scenario: At a local cafe, you joined Free_Cafe_WiFi and need to submit an assignment through your fictional university portal. Inspect the connection before entering any credentials.

instructions: You are connected to an untrusted network. Inspect the browser's security indicators before entering your credentials.
Step 2: The connection is intercepted. Choose the safest way to proceed.
hints: Secure websites encrypt your data. Check whether this connection is encrypted.
Click the padlock icon to inspect the digital certificate's issuer.

clickableRegions.explanation: Good catch - this uses http:// instead of encrypted https:// and the domain does not match the official portal.
Correct - the certificate is issued by an unknown authority, not the university's trusted issuer.
Nice observation - the urgent deadline language tries to make you sign in before checking the connection.
The page title can be copied. Check the address and certificate for stronger evidence.

options.label: Proceed anyway (the assignment is due soon!)
options.scriptedOutcome: Credentials Compromised: the simulated interceptor reads the password before it reaches the portal.

options.label: Clear browser cookies and try again
options.detail: Change a local browser setting only.
options.scriptedOutcome: Clearing cookies cannot repair a compromised router or encrypt traffic on this network.

options.label: Disconnect from WiFi and use a VPN or mobile hotspot
options.detail: Leave the untrusted path and use an encrypted connection.
options.scriptedOutcome: Secure tunnel established. The portal reloads over encrypted HTTPS.

learn.title: Treat public networks as zero trust
learn.body: The missing HTTPS, lookalike domain, and untrusted certificate each showed that this connection could not be trusted. SSL/TLS protects data in transit; a VPN or mobile hotspot adds a trusted encrypted path when public WiFi is the only option.
